findings.title: On iOS, boosts are paid through Stripe Checkout instead of IAP unless a build flag is set
findings.what: nativePromotionsEnabled() returns true only when EXPO_PUBLIC_IAP_PROMOTIONS==='1'. That variable is not set in eas.json or anywhere else in the repo. In a production iOS build nativeRail is false, so the boost purchase (paid in-app visibility, a digital service used inside the app) opens a Stripe Checkout session in an auth browser. The screen also says 'Secure payment via Stripe. You'll be redirected to complete payment.' This breaks Guideline 3.1.1, and showing an external payment mechanism breaks 3.1.3.
findings.steps: Seller account > Studio/Marketing > Boost a post > pick a post and budget > 'Boost post · $X' > Stripe Checkout opens in a browser sheet.
findings.expected: On iOS/Android, buy boosts only as App Store/Play consumables through RevenueCat. Ship with EXPO_PUBLIC_IAP_PROMOTIONS=1 and the consumables created, or hide paid boosts on native.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. nativePromotionsEnabled() requires EXPO_PUBLIC_IAP_PROMOTIONS==='1' and Repl eas.json sets no such env (production profile uses EAS 'environment: production', so it could only come from EAS dashboard env vars, not visible in source); boost falls back to Stripe openAuthSessionAsync and shows the Stripe copy.

findings.title: Calls are fully simulated in production: fake ring, fake "connected", nobody is called
findings.what: CallSessionContext hard-wires `const provider = createPreviewCallProvider()` (no network, no media). The header phone/video buttons are shown to every signed-in buyer (gated only on conv && !isAgentConv); an outgoing call "rings" for 2.2s then auto-connects and later shows "{name}'s camera is off", while the other person receives nothing. Call-log bubbles are then written into the thread. Note: a real Agora engine already exists at app/call-screen.tsx (used by manufacturer messages), so DMs are the only path left on the simulator.
findings.steps: Signed-in buyer, open a DM with a seller, tap the phone icon; have the seller watch their device.
findings.expected: Hide call buttons until a real provider (Agora) is wired, or place a real call.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. CallSessionContext hard-wires `const provider = createPreviewCallProvider()` (Repl line 25); the preview provider auto-connects after RING_MS=2200 and sets peerCameraOff after 4s with no network or media, and call logs are only local context state; the buyer-conversation gating (conv && !isAgentConv, line 2236) was checked in the local copy since that file is >100KB.

findings.title: In-feed ad campaigns are paid through Stripe Checkout on iOS (same flag defaults to off)
findings.what: design-campaign.tsx uses the same nativePromotionsEnabled() rail. With the flag unset, 'Launch · $X' opens Stripe Checkout (WebBrowser.openAuthSessionAsync). The ads are Brandthread in-feed placements shown inside the app, which makes them a digital service. Guidelines 3.1.1 and 3.1.3.
findings.steps: Seller > Marketing > Create ad > fill in creative and budget > Launch > Stripe Checkout opens.
findings.expected: Sell through IAP consumables on native, or don't offer paid ad campaigns on iOS.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. design-campaign.tsx uses the same nativeRail flag and otherwise calls api.adCampaigns.pay + WebBrowser.openAuthSessionAsync.

findings.title: Paid 'Featured' slots are always sold through Stripe Checkout, with no native IAP path
findings.what: featured-slot.tsx has no IAP rail at all. pay() reserves a slot and opens Stripe Checkout with WebBrowser.openAuthSessionAsync on every platform. Prices are $29/$59/$99 for in-app promotion on the Discover tab, which is a digital service consumed in the app. Guideline 3.1.1.
findings.steps: Seller > Boost screen > 'Featured' entry (boost.tsx:1069) > choose 3/7/14 days > 'Pay $29' > Stripe Checkout opens.
findings.expected: Use an IAP consumable/non-consumable on iOS and Android, or hide the feature on native.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. featured-slot.tsx pay() always reserves then opens Stripe Checkout via openAuthSessionAsync with no Platform/IAP branch; demo prices are $29/$59/$99.

findings.title: LegalAcceptanceGate calls a hook after an early return; it crashes when the gate needs to show
findings.what: LegalAcceptanceGate returns null when needsAgreement is false, then calls useIsWebShell() (which calls useWindowDimensions) after that return. On first render needsAgreement=false, so the hook is skipped. When check() sets needsAgreement=true, the next render runs one more hook and React throws 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render'. The React Compiler skips components that break the rules of hooks, so it does not fix this. The gate shows for every account without a recorded agreement. That includes anyone who signs up with Apple or Google from the sign-in screen, which never stores pending consent. So the first launch after Sign in with Apple crashes, or lands on the root ErrorBoundary. Guideline 2.1 (crash), and the 1.2 EULA agreement never completes.
findings.steps: Fresh install > Sign in > Continue with Apple using a new Apple ID > the account is created > the gate's check() finds no termsVersion > re-render > crash or error screen.
findings.expected: Call every hook before any conditional return (move useIsWebShell above `if (!isSignedIn || !needsAgreement) return null`). The agreement modal should then render.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. Repl has `if (!isSignedIn || !needsAgreement) return null;` at line 100 followed by `const isWebShell = useIsWebShell();` at 107, so hook count changes when needsAgreement flips true.

findings.title: Seller call buttons start a simulated call that auto-"connects" with no one

findings.steps: Seller opens a buyer DM, taps the video icon; check the buyer's device.
findings.expected: Real call or no call buttons.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. Same preview-only provider; the seller-conversation startCall (line 629) and CallLogBubble onCallBack (line 1232) were checked in the local copy (file >100KB), so seller calls auto-'connect' without ringing anyone.

findings.title: Most AI settings toggles have no effect (data sources, enable assistant, confirmations, suggestions)
findings.what: Settings are saved only to AsyncStorage and the only field read anywhere is sessionMemoryEnabled (services/aiService.ts). "Enable AI assistant", "Dashboard suggestions", "Brand Memory", all confirm-before-action toggles, and every Data source toggle (Products, Orders, Customers, ...) are never consulted, so turning off e.g. Customers does not stop the assistant from using customer data. Also device-local only, so they don't follow the seller to another device.
findings.steps: AI Settings -> turn off "Customers" data source and "Enable AI assistant"; open AI Brain and ask about customers.
findings.expected: Toggles enforced (ideally server-side) and synced to the account.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. ai-settings only writes to AsyncStorage (saveAISettings); in aiService the only setting consulted is sessionMemoryEnabled (loadSession/_persistSession), buildChatRequest always sends getEnabledMemorySummary() regardless of brandMemoryEnabled, and nothing reads enabled/suggestionsEnabled/confirm*/dataSources (local repo grep shows no other readers).

findings.title: New canvas size and imported artwork are ignored by the canvas

findings.steps: AI Studio -> New canvas -> choose a size; or Import from library and pick an image.
findings.expected: Canvas opens at that size with the imported image as a layer.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. Repl ai-studio openCanvas/importFromLibrary (and openFromCamera) push /design-canvas with { label, dims, ratio, imageUri }; design-canvas is >100KB so it was checked in the local copy, where it reads only { id, addAssetId } (line 289) and never references imageUri/dims/ratio.

findings.screen: AI tools (seller): AI Studio, Photoshoot, Background removal, Text-to-design, Assistant
findings.title: Personal data is sent to a third-party AI provider without any in-app disclosure or consent
findings.what: The privacy policy says prompts and selected content (including users' photos) are sent to 'our AI providers'. The server calls OpenAI (bg-removal, photography, mockup and other routes). No screen in the app asks for consent or explains this before the first upload: there is no AI consent string or flag anywhere in app/, components/ or lib/. Guideline 5.1.2(i) requires clear disclosure, and explicit permission, before personal data goes to a third-party AI.
findings.steps: Seller > Studio > AI Studio / AI photoshoot > upload a photo of a person > generate. There is no consent sheet.
findings.expected: Show a one-time consent sheet naming the AI provider and the data sent, record the acceptance, and allow opting out.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. privacy.md lines 41/56 disclose AI providers only in the policy; design-bg-removal.tsx posts the photo to /api/bg-removal/remove with no consent prompt, and no AI-consent flag was found (app-wide absence checked against local copy).

findings.title: The buyer notification settings screen is a non-functional mock with seller-only toggles
findings.what: The buyer Settings 'Notifications' row goes to /push-notifications. That screen holds its toggles in local useState only, makes no API call and does not persist anything. The toggles are seller-only ('New orders', 'Fulfillments', 'Setup tips', 'Timeline mentions', 'Notification badge: unfulfilled orders'). Buyers have no working way to turn push categories on or off, or to opt in or out of promotional push. The real toggle exists only in the seller screen notifications-settings.tsx. Guideline 4.5.4 (opt-out in app settings) and 2.1 (non-functional UI).
findings.steps: Buyer > Profile > Menu > Settings > Notifications > flip toggles > leave and come back: everything resets, and nothing about buyers is listed.
findings.expected: Point buyers at a real preferences screen backed by api.notificationPrefs, including the 'Promotional notifications' toggle.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. Buyer catalog 'Notifications' routes to /push-notifications, whose toggles are local useState only (no API/persistence) and are seller-oriented (New orders, Fulfillments, Setup tips, Timeline mentions, badge for unfulfilled orders); no promo opt-in there.

findings.title: The seeded App Review accounts cannot delete themselves because their seeded orders block it
findings.what: The review seed creates order 1004 as paid and 'processing', plus order 1003 as shipped 4 days ago. getDeletionBlockers() blocks a buyer with paid orders in pending/processing ('buyer_orders_awaiting_shipment'). It blocks a seller with paid orders not yet delivered that shipped less than 30 days ago. Both demo accounts therefore see 'Settle these first' with Continue disabled. REVIEW_NOTES.md tells reviewers deletion works from Settings > Delete account. Guideline 5.1.1(v).
findings.steps: Sign in as the demo buyer (or seller) > Settings > Delete account > the blocker card appears and Continue stays disabled.
findings.expected: Seed the review accounts with no open obligations (e.g. only delivered or cancelled orders), or let deletion proceed and auto-cancel/refund instead of blocking.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. Seed plan has RVW-1004 'processing' (paid) and RVW-1003 'shipped' 4 days ago; getDeletionBlockers blocks buyer on paid pending/processing orders and seller on paid undelivered orders (shipped <30d), so both demo accounts get blockers (1004 blocks both even once 1003 ages out).

findings.title: Deleting an account does not cancel the seller subscription or warn about App Store billing
findings.what: purgeAccount() deletes seller_subscription_entitlements rows but never cancels the Stripe subscription. Nothing in accountDeletion.ts or accountPurge.ts calls subscriptions.cancel. The deletion screen's 'What we delete / keep' lists and blockers never mention an active App Store or Play subscription, which keeps renewing after the account is gone. Apple expects apps to tell users how to cancel subscriptions billed through Apple (5.1.1(v), 3.1.2).
findings.steps: Seller on a paid plan > Settings > Delete account or store. There is no warning about the subscription. After 30 days the account is purged and Stripe or Apple keep charging.
findings.expected: Cancel Stripe subscriptions when deletion is scheduled. For App Store/Play subscriptions, show a notice with a link to manage or cancel in the store.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. purgeAccount only deletes seller_subscription_entitlements and nulls subscriptionId; neither it nor jobs/accountPurge.ts (path is src/jobs/, not lib/) cancels Stripe/store subscriptions, and the server-provided willDelete/willRetain lists (routes/auth.ts:299-308) never mention subscriptions.

findings.title: Passwordless accounts can only delete with an emailed code, which may fail to arrive
findings.what: getReauthMethod() returns 'email_code' for every account without a password (all Apple and Google sign-ups). issueDeletionCode() fails with MAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED when Resend is not set, and with MAIL_SEND_FAILED on a send error. For 'Hide My Email' Apple users the code goes to a privaterelay.appleid.com address and is dropped unless the sending domain is registered with Apple's Private Email Relay. Any of these leaves the user stuck at 'Enter the 6-digit code'. There is no fallback such as a fresh Apple re-auth. Guideline 5.1.1(v).

findings.title: Seller marketing broadcasts skip the promotional-push opt-in
findings.what: deliverBroadcast() publishes each broadcast with type 'seller_broadcast' and category 'announcements', and sets no pushKind. PROMOTIONAL_PUSH_TYPES does not include 'seller_broadcast' or 'announcement', so isPromotionalPush() returns false. promoConsentAllows() then lets the push through to every follower even when promo_push_opt_in=false. A seller-to-follower blast is marketing. Guideline 4.5.4 requires explicit opt-in.
findings.steps: Seller > Marketing > Push broadcast > send. A follower who never enabled promotional notifications still gets the push.
findings.expected: Pass pushKind:'promotional' in deliverBroadcast, or add 'seller_broadcast' to PROMOTIONAL_PUSH_TYPES.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. deliverBroadcast publishes type 'seller_broadcast'/category 'announcements' with no pushKind, and PROMOTIONAL_PUSH_TYPES lacks 'seller_broadcast', so promoConsentAllows returns true regardless of promo_push_opt_in (audience filter only checks push_enabled and seller_announcements pref).

findings.title: 'Manage subscription' opens the Stripe billing portal in a browser on iOS
findings.what: handleOpenPortal() has no platform check. When the subscription's effectiveProvider is 'stripe' (a seller who subscribed on the web), getBillingRecoveryTarget returns 'stripe' and the app opens api.seller.subscription.portal() with Linking.openURL on iOS. In the Stripe customer portal the user can change plans, upgrade and update cards. That is an external purchase mechanism reached from the app (Guidelines 3.1.1 and 3.1.3). billing.tsx already blocks this on native, so the two screens disagree.
findings.steps: Sign in on iOS as a seller who subscribed on web > Settings > Subscription > 'Manage subscription' or 'Manage billing' > Safari opens the Stripe portal.
findings.expected: On native, never open the Stripe portal. Show 'Manage your plan at brandthread.app' as plain text (no link), or use the App Store management URL only for RevenueCat subscriptions.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. handleOpenPortal() has no Platform check; when getBillingRecoveryTarget returns 'stripe' it opens api.seller.subscription.portal() via Linking.openURL on native too.

findings.title: Unblock account never completes on web
findings.what: Uses lib/safety.ts confirmBlock/confirmUnblock or lib/actionSheet.ts confirmDestructiveActionSheet, which on non-iOS fall back to Alert.alert with button callbacks (lib/safety.ts:143,172; lib/actionSheet.ts:36). On react-native-web Alert.alert is a no-op, so the returned Promise never resolves (onDismiss never fires either): no dialog, no block/unblock, and the awaiting handler hangs.
findings.steps: In the web build open /buyer-blocked and tap Unblock account.
findings.expected: A confirmation appears on web and the block/unblock/delete is performed (or cancelled) and the promise resolves.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. unblock() sets pendingId then awaits confirmUnblock (Alert.alert-only in lib/safety.ts:172); on web the promise never resolves, so the button spins forever and all other Unblock buttons stay disabled; works on iOS.

findings.title: Delete/decline request (confirmDestructiveActionSheet), Block, Unblock never completes on web
findings.what: Uses lib/safety.ts confirmBlock/confirmUnblock or lib/actionSheet.ts confirmDestructiveActionSheet, which on non-iOS fall back to Alert.alert with button callbacks (lib/safety.ts:143,172; lib/actionSheet.ts:36). On react-native-web Alert.alert is a no-op, so the returned Promise never resolves (onDismiss never fires either): no dialog, no block/unblock, and the awaiting handler hangs.

findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. Repl file is >100KB (unreadable via tool); verified against local copy: 869 is handleBlockRequest (Block request, not delete/decline) via confirmDestructiveActionSheet, 1509/1518 are Unblock/Block items in a web-safe showActionSheet menu that then await Alert-only confirmUnblock/confirmBlock, and 2419 is BlockedComposer's Unblock; all never resolve on web, work on iOS.

findings.steps: Open the web build, navigate to tabs)/products, trigger: Delete product.
findings.expected: A cross-platform confirmation (in-app modal/sheet or window.confirm on web) appears and the confirmed action executes.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. handleDelete (used by action sheet and swipe quick-delete) deletes only inside Alert.alert 'Delete product?' onPress, no web branch; dead on web, works on iOS.

findings.title: Block seller never completes on web
findings.what: Uses lib/safety.ts confirmBlock/confirmUnblock or lib/actionSheet.ts confirmDestructiveActionSheet, which on non-iOS fall back to Alert.alert with button callbacks (lib/safety.ts:143,172; lib/actionSheet.ts:36). On react-native-web Alert.alert is a no-op, so the returned Promise never resolves (onDismiss never fires either): no dialog, no block/unblock, and the awaiting handler hangs.
findings.steps: In the web build open /seller-profile and tap Block seller.
findings.expected: A confirmation appears on web and the block/unblock/delete is performed (or cancelled) and the promise resolves.
findings.verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. The '...' menu is a ProfileMenuSheet, but its Block item awaits confirmBlock (Alert.alert-only in lib/safety.ts), which never resolves on web; works on iOS.

findings.title: The sign-in screen creates accounts through Apple/Google with no Terms or Privacy link and no consent stored
findings.what: sign-in.tsx offers 'Continue with Apple' and 'Continue with Google'. With Clerk SSO these create brand-new accounts. The screen has no LegalContinueNotice, no Terms/Privacy link and never calls rememberPendingConsent(). New users from this path get no agreement until the LegalAcceptanceGate, which currently crashes (see the P0 finding). Guidelines 1.2 (EULA before UGC) and 5.1.1(i) (privacy policy reachable at sign-up).
findings.steps: Fresh install > Sign in > look for Terms/Privacy links next to the Apple/Google buttons.
findings.expected: Show the same 'By continuing you agree to…' notice with tappable Terms, Privacy and Guidelines links on the sign-in screen.
findings.verified: UNVERIFIED against the live Repl (only P0/P1 static claims were re-checked); found in the reconstructed source.

findings.title: Agreement to the EULA and community rules is browsewrap, with no affirmative action
findings.what: Account creation records consent implicitly: rememberPendingConsent() runs on 'Continue' and the screen shows a LegalContinueNotice line. LegalAcceptanceGate then sends that stored pending consent to the server automatically, so the user never actively agrees to the zero-tolerance terms. Reviewers often ask for an explicit agreement to the terms or EULA in UGC apps (Guideline 1.2).
findings.steps: Fresh install > Create account > email/password > Continue. There is no checkbox or 'I agree' step.
findings.expected: Add an explicit checkbox or 'I agree' tap before account creation for UGC users.
findings.verified: UNVERIFIED against the live Repl (only P0/P1 static claims were re-checked); found in the reconstructed source.

findings.title: Production web bundle is one 12.8 MB JS chunk (3.4 MB gzipped)
findings.what: `expo export --platform web` of the current code produces a single 12.8 MB `index-*.js` (3.41 MB gzipped) that every visitor downloads before first paint; the remaining 4 chunks are <50 KB, so route-level code splitting is effectively not happening. On a mid-range phone over 4G this is several seconds of download + parse before the first screen.
findings.steps: `pnpm --filter @workspace/mobile exec expo export --platform web` and inspect `dist/_expo/static/js/web`.
findings.expected: Lazy route bundles (Expo Router async routes) so the first screen ships < 1 MB gzipped; heavy screens (Design Studio, AI, Live, Manufacturer) load on demand.

findings.title: ~46 MB of demo-feed videos ship inside the app bundle
findings.what: Ten `assets/videos/fashion_runway_*.mp4` files (4.4–5.0 MB each) are `require()`d statically by the preview/demo feed data, so they are bundled into every build (web export assets total 103 MB; they would also inflate the iOS binary/OTA update) even though they are only shown in demo/preview mode.
findings.steps: Build the web export or an iOS archive and list bundled assets.
findings.expected: Demo media served from a CDN (or excluded from production builds); production bundle contains no demo-only media.
findings.source: artifacts/mobile/lib/previewFeed.ts and other preview*.ts files that require ../../assets/videos/*.mp4

findings.title: The contacts purpose string says contacts are 'never uploaded', but hashed contacts are uploaded
findings.what: NSContactsUsageDescription says 'your contact list is never uploaded or stored'. The app hashes every email and phone and POSTs up to 6,000 SHA-256 hashes to /api/social/contacts/match. Unsalted hashes of phone numbers can be reversed, and the privacy manifest declares Contacts as collected. The privacy policy never mentions contacts. Guideline 5.1.1 (accurate purpose strings and policy).
findings.steps: Read the iOS permission prompt and compare it with the network traffic from Find friends.
findings.expected: Reword to 'only scrambled codes (hashes) are sent to check matches and aren't stored', and add contact matching to privacy.md.
findings.verified: UNVERIFIED against the live Repl (only P0/P1 static claims were re-checked); found in the reconstructed source.
